headline: Swansea lead the Championship; the market still favours QPR
summary: Swansea arrive at Loftus Road top of the Championship with 23 points from 11 games, yet the market makes QPR the more likely winners. QPR's win chance rose from 37.5% to 40.4% in recent days, while Swansea are given 31.5%. Swansea's winning run ended with a 1-0 home defeat to West Ham on Saturday, and QPR lost 0-3 at Birmingham. Yahoo Sports reports QPR are without Ilias Chair, their attacking midfielder.
read: Swansea travel to Loftus Road top of the Championship, but the market rates QPR the more likely winners at 40.4% to 31.5% — home advantage outweighing the eight-place gap. QPR are without four senior players including Ilias Chair and have won once in five, while Swansea's four-match winning run ended with a 1-0 home defeat to West Ham on Saturday; the price has moved towards the home side anyway, and the goals line sits almost level at 2.45.

facts.fact: Swansea arrive at Loftus Road top of the Championship with 23 points from 11 games.
facts.meaning: The division's front-runners are the visitors, which makes QPR's status as market favourite the story of the game.

facts.fact: The market makes QPR the more likely winner at 40.4%, against Swansea's 31.5% and 28.1% for the draw.
facts.meaning: The side eight places lower in the table is rated the likelier winner — home advantage is doing the work.

facts.fact: QPR's win chance has risen from 37.5% to 40.4% in recent days.
facts.meaning: The market has strengthened the home side and now rates QPR a fraction of a goal the better team.

facts.fact: QPR are without Nicolas Madsen, Rumarn Burrell and Tariq Lamptey until after the November international break, and Ilias Chair is ruled out of the Swansea match.
facts.meaning: Four senior options unavailable, including Chair — QPR's usual attacking midfielder (background) — so the home side's squad is stretched.

facts.fact: Amadou Mbengue has suffered a major injury expected to keep him out for a long layoff.
facts.meaning: Another long-term loss for QPR, thinning the defensive options further.

facts.fact: QPR lost 0-3 away at Birmingham on 17 October.
facts.meaning: One win in their last five (LWDDD) — a home side in so-so form being asked to beat the league leaders.

facts.fact: Swansea's 1-0 home defeat to West Ham on Saturday ended a four-match winning run.
facts.meaning: The leaders lost for the first time in five and come to London off a blank at home.

facts.fact: Swansea average 1.76 xG per game this run of five, against QPR's 1.42.

sources.fact: QPR will be without Nicolas Madsen, Rumarn Burrell and Tariq Lamptey until after the November international break, and Ilias Chair has been ruled out of the Swansea match.
Amadou Mbengue has suffered a major injury that is expected to keep him out for a long layoff, with QPR boss Julien Stephan losing a key player for the rest of the Championship campaign.
Richard Kone has been given the all-clear after an injury scare and is expected to be available for the home game against Swansea.
QPR lost 3-0 away at Birmingham City in their previous Championship match, a result that dropped them from fifth to ninth in the table.
Before the Birmingham defeat QPR had lost just one of their first 10 matches and were in the top eight of the Championship.
Swansea's four-match winning streak was ended by a 1-0 home defeat to West Ham United, which cut their lead at the top of the Championship to a single point.
Swansea go into the match as Championship leaders, having led the table before the West Ham defeat reduced their advantage to one point.
Swansea are relaxed about reports linking manager Vitor Matos with Crystal Palace, with no approach or contact made by the Premier League club.
